big_idea: We name attributes, compare and order objects, and use a calendar to mark our measurement day.
learning_intention: We are learning to use measurement and the calendar together.
student_learning_goal: I can use measurement and the calendar together.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Roo and Cal — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.

minds_on.activity_name: Roo and Cal Plan Measurement Day
minds_on.hook: Roo: Today is MEASUREMENT DAY! 4 stations: NAME the attribute, ORDER by length, ORDER by mass, READ the calendar! Roo opens: 'Measure it!' Class: 'Match it!' Cal: 'Mark the day!'
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Roo and Cal puppets in lab coats. 'Friends — today is our CAPSTONE. We use ALL we know: attributes, comparisons, calendar.'

Review each idea quickly. 'Attributes — length, area, mass, capacity. Compare — line up, cover, balance, pour. Calendar — days, weeks, months, holidays, seasons.'

Now show 4 stations:
- Station 1: NAME — pick an object, name 2 attributes.
- Station 2: ORDER LENGTH — order 4 strips shortest to longest.
- Station 3: ORDER MASS — balance 4 objects, order lightest to heaviest.
- Station 4: CALENDAR — find today's date, name a holiday and a season.

Each child rotates through all 4 stations and records on the CAPSTONE TEMPLATE.

'Roo and Cal say — every measurement detective uses ALL these skills. Today YOU prove you can.'

'Welcome to MEASUREMENT DAY!'

steps.instruction: WHOLE GROUP: Roo + Cal review Day 1-4 success criteria. Class chants the unit refrain: 'Measure it! / Match it! / Mark the day!'
steps.teacher_prompt: Roo: 'Today you do all four things — name the attribute, compare two, order many, and mark the day.'

steps.instruction: Station 1 — NAME THE ATTRIBUTE: 8 mixed objects. Pair names the attribute to measure for each. Pair compares with another pair: any disagreements? Why?
steps.teacher_prompt: Roo: 'A backpack has MASS and CAPACITY. The MATH word picks one you can measure.'

steps.instruction: Station 2 — ORDER BY LENGTH (transitivity): pair has 4 objects. They compare pairs and order all 4. Conceptual prompts: 'How do you KNOW C is longer than D? Did you line up the ends?' / 'If C is longer than B and B is longer than D, what does that tell you about C and D?'
steps.teacher_prompt: Roo: 'Sort by length. Use a chain — if A beats B, and B beats C, A beats C. No re-checking.'

steps.instruction: Station 3 — ORDER BY MASS (sense-making): pair has 4 objects of similar size but different mass (water bottle, brick fragment, sponge, pencil case). Conceptual prompts: 'Water bottle vs brick — which has more MASS? More CAPACITY? How do you know?' Pair uses balance OR two-handed heft test.
steps.teacher_prompt: Roo: 'Some things look big but feel light. Mass isn't size — it's HEFT.'

steps.instruction: Station 4 — MARK THE DAY: Cal's calendar. Pair finds today's date, counts forward 5 days to find when the Measurement Day project will be complete.
steps.teacher_prompt: Cal: 'Mark the day! Math doesn't just measure THINGS — it measures TIME.'

steps.instruction: Circulate to record formative evidence on the capstone rubric. Surface transitivity gaps, attribute confusion, calendar-counting errors.

differentiation.for_extending: After all 4 stations, write a 'big conclusion' about what you learned this week.
differentiation.for_ell_or_iep: Provide pre-printed sentence frames on the template.
differentiation.for_movement_learners: Walk between 4 station tables, physically engage at each. NO-PREP STATION PATH: Station 2 — order any 4 classroom objects by length using the baseboard as alignment line. Station 3 — order 4 objects by mass using two-handed heft test if no balance available. Station 4 — point to today on a single class wall calendar; no per-pair calendars needed.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Four signals: names attributes; orders 4 by length; orders 4 by mass; reads calendar.

discussion_prompts: What's the difference between mass and capacity?
What did you learn about the calendar?
How would you measure a desk?
consolidation.exit_routine: Roo + Cal closing refrain — Roo: 'Measure it!' Class: 'Match it!' Cal: 'Mark the day!' Repeat 3x. Each child shares one object they ordered and the attribute they used.

assessment_in_this_lesson.rationale: Lesson 5 captures E2.1 + E2.2 + E2.3 in one capstone.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child loses the transitivity chain — repairing the A>B, B>C ⇒ A>C gap
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
On the capstone where children must order 4+ objects by length OR mass, the dominant Grade-1 measurement trap is the transitivity gap (Sarama & Clements 2009, Piaget's seriation work): child directly compares A>B and B>C but cannot infer A>C without physically rechecking. Closely related is attribute confusion — child orders by LENGTH when asked about MASS (because length is easier to see).

Today integrates Lessons 1-4: NAME the attribute (L1), DIRECTLY compare two (L2-3), ORDER many using transitivity (today), and MARK the day on the calendar (L4).
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Pair has 4 objects of varying length on Station 2's mat. Child has compared object A vs B (A longer) and B vs C (B longer). Teacher asks: 'is A longer than C?' Child says 'I'll have to check.'
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'You showed me A is longer than B. You showed me B is longer than C. So... what about A and C?'

If child rechecks: 'You're right that checking is safe. Let me show you a math shortcut. If A beats B, and B beats C, then A MUST beat C. Without measuring again. That's transitive reasoning.'

Re-state with three blocks: 'Block A wins against block B. Block B wins against block C. So block A...?' Child completes 'wins against block C.'

Long-term recovery: every ordering task has a 'predict, then check' step — child predicts using transitivity, then verifies.
expected_student_responses: (Mid) Hesitates, then says 'A beats C... I think.'
(Strong) States A beats C immediately and explains via B.
(Stretched) Orders all 4 objects from a single round of pairwise comparisons.
common_misconceptions: Cannot transit comparisons (A>B, B>C ⇒ A>C). (Repair: model the chain.)
Orders by visible attribute (length) when asked about hidden one (mass). (Repair: re-name the attribute first, then re-order.)
Re-measures every pair instead of using prior comparisons. (Repair: 'predict, then check.')
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child rechecks every pair: model the transitive chain with three blocks; child says 'A>B, B>C, so A>C' aloud before any rechecking.
DIAGNOSTIC B — child orders by visible attribute (length) when asked about hidden (mass): re-name the attribute first ('we are asking about MASS, not LENGTH'), then re-order using a balance.
DIAGNOSTIC C — child cannot start ordering at all: drop to two objects only, name the attribute, name the comparison, then add a third object.

worksheet_brief.purpose: Summative artifact applying E2.1 + E2.2 + E2.3.

parts_outline.task: NAME: pick 2 objects. Write 2 attributes for each.
ORDER: 4 strips by length. 4 objects by mass.
CALENDAR: find today's date. Name a holiday and its season.
